cosing_function: Antioxidant; Skin conditioning
brief_description: Pure form of vitamin C; scavenges free radicals and helps brighten skin tone and support collagen,  but is unstable and can irritate at high strength.

cosing_function: Antioxidant; Skin conditioning
brief_description: A stabilized,  water-soluble vitamin C derivative that converts to ascorbic acid in skin; gentler and more shelf-stable than pure vitamin C.

cosing_function: Skin conditioning - humectant; Antioxidant
brief_description: Stable,  water-soluble vitamin C derivative with added anti-acne/antibacterial benefit; converts slowly to active ascorbic acid in skin.

cosing_function: Skin conditioning; Antioxidant
brief_description: Stable vitamin C derivative favored for sensitive or oily skin; supports collagen synthesis and mild brightening with lower irritation risk.

cosing_function: Skin conditioning
brief_description: Gold-standard OTC retinoid; converts in-skin to retinoic acid to speed cell turnover,  boost collagen,  and fade fine lines/pigmentation. Regulated under EU Annex III concentration limits.

cosing_function: Skin conditioning
brief_description: Ester of retinol and palmitic acid; the mildest,  most stable retinoid ester,  needs more conversion steps in skin so it is gentler but less potent than retinol.

cosing_function: Skin conditioning (reported; not separately confirmed in CosIng search)
brief_description: Intermediate between retinol and retinoic acid in the conversion pathway; considered more potent than retinol with a faster visible effect,  still one enzymatic step gentler than prescription retinoic acid.

cosing_function: Retinoids
cas_number: N/A - regulated as a drug/OTC monograph actives, not a CosIng cosmetic ingredient
brief_description: Differin, Third-generation synthetic retinoid; prescription/OTC-drug status (not CosIng-listed) because it is regulated as a therapeutic drug in the EU and US,  not a cosmetic. Included here as a labeling note only.

cosing_function: Skin conditioning; Soothing agent
brief_description: Multitasking actives that strengthens the skin barrier,  reduces redness/inflammation,  regulates sebum,  and fades post-acne marks; pairs well with most other actives.

cosing_function: Antiseborrhoeic agent; Keratolytic agent; Skin conditioning
brief_description: Oil-soluble beta hydroxy acid that penetrates into sebum-filled pores to exfoliate and unclog them; standard acne and blackhead treatment.

cosing_function: Skin conditioning - exfoliant (reported)
brief_description: Smallest-molecule AHA,  derived from sugarcane; penetrates deepest for strong resurfacing,  brightening,  and collagen stimulation but carries the highest irritation risk of the AHAs.

cosing_function: Skin conditioning - humectant; exfoliant (reported)
brief_description: Milder AHA (from milk/fermentation) that exfoliates gently while also acting as a humectant,  improving barrier hydration alongside resurfacing.

cosing_function: Skin conditioning - exfoliant (reported)
brief_description: Larger-molecule AHA from bitter almonds; slower,  more even exfoliation with added antibacterial/anti-inflammatory action,  well tolerated by sensitive and acne-prone skin.

cosing_function: Antimicrobial (drug-classified acne treatment; not a core CosIng cosmetic function)
brief_description: Topical antiseptic that releases free radicals to kill acne-causing bacteria (C. acnes) and has mild keratolytic/sebostatic effects; in the EU it is regulated closer to a drug actives than a standard cosmetic ingredient.

cosing_function: Skin conditioning; Antimicrobial (reported)
brief_description: Naturally derived dicarboxylic acid with antimicrobial,  anti-inflammatory,  and tyrosinase-inhibiting action; used for acne,  rosacea redness,  and post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation.

cosing_function: Skin conditioning - humectant
brief_description: High-molecular-weight humectant naturally found in skin; binds large amounts of water at the surface to plump and hydrate,  but does not penetrate deeply due to molecule size.

cosing_function: Skin conditioning - humectant
brief_description: Salt form of hyaluronic acid; smaller and more water-soluble than HA itself,  so it penetrates slightly deeper while retaining strong water-binding capacity (up to ~1000x its weight).

cosing_function: Skin conditioning - occlusive (general family function; not individually confirmed in CosIng search)
brief_description: One of the most abundant ceramides in the skin's own lipid barrier; replenishes barrier lipids to reduce water loss and improve barrier repair. Data here is PubChem/industry-sourced,  not directly confirmed via CosIng search.

cosing_function: Skin conditioning - occlusive (not independently verified this session)
brief_description: Long-chain,  esterified ceramide that forms part of the skin's outer lipid lamellae; supports barrier structure. CAS/CosIng not verified in this pass - flagged for manual check.

cosing_function: Skin conditioning - occlusive (not independently verified this session)
brief_description: Barrier lipid ceramide commonly blended with Ceramide NP/EOP in "ceramide complex" formulations mimicking natural skin lipid ratios. CAS/CosIng not verified in this pass - flagged for manual check.

cosing_function: Skin conditioning (signal peptide; not separately itemized in CosIng search)
brief_description: Signal peptide (5 amino acids + palmitic acid chain) that "tricks" fibroblasts into producing more collagen and hyaluronic acid; well-studied anti-wrinkle ingredient effective at very low doses.

cosing_function: Skin conditioning (general peptide category; not verified this session)
brief_description: Broad category note: copper peptides (e.g.,  GHK-Cu) are reported to support wound healing,  collagen/elastin production,  and antioxidant enzyme activity. This is a general category summary,  not a single verified CosIng entry - treat CAS/function as unconfirmed.

cosing_function: Skin conditioning (reported; tyrosinase inhibitor not itemized separately in CosIng search)
brief_description: Synthetic,  more stable isomer of arbutin; inhibits tyrosinase to reduce melanin production,  used for hyperpigmentation and skin brightening with lower irritation than hydroquinone.

cosing_function: Skin conditioning
brief_description: Works via the plasmin pathway rather than direct tyrosinase inhibition; blocks UV- and hormone-triggered melanocyte signaling,  making it especially effective for melasma and UV-driven pigmentation.

cosing_function: Skin conditioning (reported; tyrosinase inhibitor not itemized separately in CosIng search)
brief_description: Fungal-fermentation-derived tyrosinase inhibitor that chelates copper at the enzyme's active site to reduce melanin production; also has antioxidant activity,  but is more prone to instability/irritation than arbutin.

cosing_function: Bulking; Cosmetic colorant (CI 77947); Skin protecting; UV absorber; UV filter
brief_description: Physical/mineral UV filter that sits on the skin surface and reflects/scatters UVA and UVB rather than absorbing it chemically; also used at lower levels as a skin-protecting agent and white colorant. One of only two sunscreen actives (with Titanium Dioxide) the FDA classifies GRASE (safe and effective) up to 25% concentration; EU prohibits nano-ZnO in spray or powder cosmetic formats.

cosing_function: Cosmetic colorant (White, CI 77891); Opacifier; UV absorber; UV filter
brief_description: Physical/mineral UV filter that reflects and scatters UVA and UVB; also the most common white pigment/opacifier in cosmetics generally. FDA GRASE up to 25%, alongside Zinc Oxide. Inhalable powder/nano forms carry a separate GHS respiratory and carcinogenicity caution that applies to loose powder or spray products, not standard cream-based topical sunscreen.

cosing_function: UV filter; Antioxidant (reported)
brief_description: The only organic UV filter providing strong broad-spectrum UVA1/UVA2 absorption (EU Annex VI entry 8, max 5%; US max 3%); chemically unstable and photodegrades under UV exposure unless paired with a stabilizer (commonly Octocrylene), losing SPF potency over the day and forming breakdown products (arylglyoxals, benzils) linked in the literature to occasional photoallergic reactions.

cosing_function: Light stabilizer; UV absorber; UV filter
common_synonyms: Ethylhexyl Methoxycinnamate; Octyl Methoxycinnamate; OMC; EHMC
brief_description: UVB-only chemical filter (peak absorption ~310nm); one of the most widely used sunscreen actives globally. US max 7.5%; the EU's SCCS concluded in 2025 that EHMC is safe as a UV filter up to 10% including in children. Frequently combined with UVA filters like Avobenzone for broad-spectrum coverage.

cosing_function: Light stabilizer; UV absorber; UV filter
brief_description: Oil-soluble UVB/short-UVA chemical filter (US max 10%) valued mainly as a photostabilizer for Avobenzone (raises its photostability from roughly 23% to 90% remaining after UV exposure); also used at low levels (0.2-0.5%) as a non-sunscreen light stabilizer in nail products. Long believed non-sensitizing, but recent dermatology literature documents a rising rate of contact and photocontact allergy, some cross-reacting with ketoprofen/benzophenone-3.

cosing_function: Skin conditioning; UV absorber; UV filter
brief_description: Salicylate-based UVB chemical filter (peak ~306nm) also used as a solvent that helps dissolve less-soluble UV filters into a formula; not photostable on its own. Permitted to 15% in the US and 10% in the EU. SCCS review has flagged possible endocrine-disrupting activity as an open question, and the EU is re-assessing its concentration limits.

cosing_function: Skin conditioning (reported; not itemized as a distinct function in CosIng search)
common_synonyms: Argireline; Acetyl Hexapeptide-3; Acetyl Hexapeptide-8 Amide
brief_description: Synthetic hexapeptide marketed as a topical 'Botox alternative': competes for a position in the SNARE/SNAP-25 vesicle-fusion complex to modestly reduce neurotransmitter release at the neuromuscular junction, softening expression lines. CIR's safe-use conclusion applies only up to 0.005% -- far below the 10% used in some clinical efficacy trials, so real-world leave-on products are dosed nowhere near the concentrations that generated the headline efficacy data.

cosing_function: Skin conditioning (reported; general peptide category function, not separately itemized in CosIng search)
common_synonyms: Palmitoyl Oligopeptide (retired INCI name); Pal-GHK; Palmitoyl-GHK Tripeptide; Matrixyl 3000 (component)
brief_description: Palmitic-acid-conjugated fragment of the GHK collagen-signal peptide; co-formulated with Palmitoyl Tetrapeptide-7 as 'Matrixyl 3000' to stimulate collagen I/III/IV and fibronectin synthesis. Previously sold under the INCI name 'Palmitoyl Oligopeptide', which the INCI dictionary retired for being too vague (it covered more than one undefined peptide sequence) -- treat that older name as a legacy/indirect match, not an exact one.

cosing_function: Skin conditioning (reported; general peptide category function, not separately itemized in CosIng search)
brief_description: Palmitic-acid-conjugated GQPR signal peptide; the second half of the 'Matrixyl 3000' blend alongside Palmitoyl Tripeptide-1. Used at very low levels (typically under 10ppm) to signal fibroblasts toward collagen/ECM production and reported to modulate inflammatory (IL-6) signaling associated with skin aging.

cosing_function: Antistatic; Hair conditioning; Skin conditioning
common_synonyms: Pro-Vitamin B5; Pantothenol; Dexpanthenol/D-Panthenol (single-enantiomer form, CAS 81-13-0 -- not independently re-verified this pass)
brief_description: Alcohol form of pantothenic acid (vitamin B5); converts to pantothenic acid in skin, where it improves hydration/water retention, supports barrier repair, and has mild anti-inflammatory/itch-soothing effects. Extremely well tolerated; one of the most common 'safe to pair with anything' actives, often included specifically to offset irritation from retinoids or acids.

cosing_function: Skin conditioning - emollient
brief_description: Fully saturated (hydrogenated) form of squalene, a lipid naturally present in human sebum; used as a lightweight, non-comedogenic emollient that reduces transepidermal water loss without the oxidative instability of unsaturated squalene. Plant-derived (olive, sugarcane) sourcing has largely replaced the older shark-liver-oil source. Compatible with essentially all other actives; commonly used to cushion irritation from retinoids, acids, or benzoyl peroxide.

cosing_function: Skin conditioning - humectant; Smoothing; Soothing; Tonic
common_synonyms: Cica; Gotu Kola Extract; Tiger Grass Extract
brief_description: Botanical extract standardized for triterpenoid actives (asiaticoside, madecassoside, asiatic acid, madecassic acid) with anti-inflammatory, wound-healing, and mild collagen-supportive effects; widely marketed as 'Cica' in barrier-repair and post-procedure/soothing formulas. As a whole-plant extract it is not a single defined chemical (see pubchem_safety.csv note), so composition and potency vary by supplier and extraction method.

cosing_function: Antioxidant; Emollient; Skin conditioning (reported via secondary ingredient databases; not independently confirmed via direct CosIng search this pass)
brief_description: Plant-derived (Psoralea corylifolia seed) meroterpenoid marketed as a gentler alternative to retinol. The key head-to-head RCT (Dhaliwal et al., Br J Dermatol 2019) found 0.5% bakuchiol twice-daily produced statistically comparable improvement in wrinkles and hyperpigmentation to 0.5% retinol every day/every-other-day over 12 weeks, with significantly LESS scaling and stinging reported in the bakuchiol arm. It appears to upregulate similar collagen genes (COL1A1/COL3A1) and downregulate MMPs, but through a different mechanism than direct retinoic-acid-receptor binding -- so it is a reasonable retinoid-intolerant substitute, not a proven pharmacological equivalent.

cosing_function: Skin conditioning
brief_description: Small soothing/healing molecule (a purine metabolite, also found in comfrey root) that increases skin smoothness, has mild keratolytic action encouraging shedding of dead surface cells, and calms irritation; one of the most established de-sensitizing additives, commonly included alongside stronger actives (acids, retinoids, benzoyl peroxide) specifically to offset their irritation. CIR-safe up to 2%.
